passages.titleJp: わたしの日曜日[にちようび]

translationEn: Since the modern era, both academia and industry have achieved remarkable results by advancing subdivision and specialization. There is no doubt that digging deeply into a single domain dramatically expanded human knowledge.

translationEn: In recent large-scale urban redevelopments, profitability and ease of management tend to take priority, assigning a clear function to every square meter. A city designed down to the last gap—commercial zones, pedestrian corridors, paid lounges—appears comfortable and attractive at first glance.

Yet spaces whose uses are strictly prescribed rarely foster serendipitous encounters or experimental endeavors. What historically sustained urban vitality was never polished facilities alone, but the presence of "blank spaces" such as undefined plazas and back alleys.

Design obsessed solely with efficiency may yield short-term returns, yet in the long run risks stripping a city of its unique culture. Deliberately leaving blank spaces without predetermined functions is an essential condition for a city to keep renewing itself organically.

しかし逆[ぎゃく]に言[い]えば、完全[かんぜん]な置き換[おきか]えができないからこそ、翻訳者[ほんやくしゃ]は自国[じこく]の言葉[ことば]の限界[げんかい]と向[む]き合[あ]い、新[あら]たな表現[ひょうげん]を搾[しぼ]り出[だ]さざるを得[え]ない。翻訳[ほんやく]とは単[たん]なる意味[いみ]の伝達[でんたつ]にとどまらず、受[う]け入[い]れ側[がわ]の言語[げんご]そのものを揺[ゆ]さぶり、豊[ゆた]かに耕[たがや]す創造[そうぞう]行為[こうい]なのである。
translationEn: When transferring a literary work written in one language into another, it is fundamentally impossible to reproduce every nuance of the original's cadence and cultural implications without remainder. For this reason, translation has often been called a "betrayal."

Conversely, however, precisely because exact substitution is impossible, translators are forced to confront the limits of their own language and wring out fresh expressions. Translation does not stop at mere transmission of meaning; it is a creative act that shakes up and richly cultivates the receiving language itself.

paragraphsB: 文化財[ぶんかざい]のデジタル記録[きろく]が保存[ほぞん]や学術[がくじゅつ]研究[けんきゅう]に計[はか]り知[し]れない恩恵[おんけい]をもたらすことは疑[うたが]いようがない。しかしながら、「デジタルで十分[じゅうぶん]体験[たいかん]できるから実物[じつぶつ]の公開[こうかい]は原則[げんそく]不要[ふよう]」という論調[ろんちょう]には危惧[きぐ]を覚[おぼ]える。

translationEn: National-treasure murals and historic structures deteriorate daily from visitors' breath and lighting. Digital restoration using high-resolution scanning and VR is a groundbreaking means of protecting originals strictly while opening every detail to people worldwide.

By letting viewers experience brushwork invisible to the naked eye and reconstructed lost colors, digital exhibitions possess educational value that goes beyond being a mere substitute for the real thing.
translationBEn: There is no doubt that digital archiving of cultural assets brings immeasurable benefits to preservation and scholarly research. Yet I feel uneasy about rhetoric claiming that "since digital experiences suffice, displaying originals is in principle unnecessary."

The atmosphere and sense of awe felt when standing before an authentic object that survives after centuries of wear cannot be fully replaced no matter how high the resolution. Digital tools should be positioned as complements deepening interest in originals, and controlled limited viewings remain indispensable.
